lines.text: When you dial nine-one-one from your mobile phone in an emergency, how does the dispatcher pinpoint your location?
Unlike landlines tied to fixed street addresses, mobile phones move constantly.
When you place the call, cell towers instantly initiate Enhanced 911 protocol.
Your carrier triangulates radio pings from neighboring towers to narrow down your area to a block.
Simultaneously, modern smartphones activate high-accuracy GPS, Wi-Fi beacons, and barometric sensors.
The barometric pressure sensor measures vertical elevation to tell dispatchers which floor of a high-rise building you are on.
Always state your exact address first in any emergency to help responders arrive as fast as possible.
